title: Senior Advisor, Offtake & Grid Integration
description:
**Job Type:** Full-Time, Remote  
**Salary:** Negotiable, up to $130,000  
**Reports to:** Mike O’Connor, Deputy Director of Energy for Geothermal

Organization Description

The Mountain West Geothermal Consortium (MWGC) is a state-led initiative working to accelerate geothermal energy development across Colorado, Utah, New Mexico, and Arizona. The Consortium brings together state energy offices, developers, investors, utilities, insurers, and research institutions around a shared goal: removing the policy, financing, and market barriers that prevent geothermal from scaling in one of the most resource-rich regions in the world.

The Mountain West is uniquely positioned to lead a national geothermal buildout. States in the region host the nation’s early demonstrations, benefit from deep subsurface expertise and established supply chains, and contain some of the most promising geologic conditions for next-generation geothermal development—including enhanced geothermal systems (EGS). At the same time, high upfront exploration costs, limited early-stage capital, and the absence of standardized frameworks for project derisking and offtake continue to slow deployment.

The Consortium’s work is organized around three core intervention areas: a drilling derisking mechanism to backstop appraisal well costs and reduce early-stage investment risk; a public data modernization effort to improve access to subsurface resource data for developers; and a utility engagement workstream to create durable pathways for geothermal offtake through IRP inclusion, interconnection access, and improved contracting structures. The Consortium is staffed and managed by CPE and Constructive, and is funded by philanthropic support.

Position Summary

The Senior Advisor, Offtake & Grid Integration will lead the design and refinement of the Mountain West Geothermal Consortium’s utility engagement and offtake workstream—a priority area focused on creating durable pathways for geothermal power purchase
